display_name: Durably roll back to the prior release
description: Operator-triggered durable code rollback for local blue-green self-deployment. DISTINCT from swap_rollback (the in-drain-window router re-point): this brings the prior MATERIALIZED release's code back up as a fresh process and atomically flips the durable current/previous release symlinks, so it works at ANY time — post-drain, post-reboot — because both code trees persist on disk. Mechanism (PATH A): read the ledger's previous release, spawn it as the opposite color, wait for it to register + health-probe, activate it on the router, swap the current/previous symlinks (ReleaseManager.rollback), quiesce the broken current, enqueue a durable complete_swap finisher. Takes reason, expected_etag, and expected_current_release — the concurrency CAS: the rel-<id> the caller observed as current; a mismatch (a concurrent deploy/rollback moved current) returns FAILED(stale_current_release) before any spawn, with the actual current echoed for retry. Returns a RestartResult envelope whose status partitions outcomes: queued (rollback scheduled), failed (system unchanged + retryable — stale current release, no rollback target, activate refused, or a swap that compensated cleanly), or needs_intervention (automated recovery exhausted, a human must act — the rollback target will not boot, or a compensation could not complete). A second rollback_release rolls forward again (undo/redo).
embedding_description: Durably roll back local the solet to the previous materialized code release. Distinct from swap_rollback's in-window router re-point: brings the prior release's code tree back up and flips the durable current/previous symlinks, so it works at any time including after the drain window or a reboot. Spawns previous as the opposite color, activates, swaps symlinks, enqueues complete_swap. Takes reason + expected_current_release (a concurrency CAS against the live current release); returns a RestartResult with status (queued/failed/needs_intervention) and a machine-readable reason_code (stale_current_release, no_rollback_target, activate_refused, rollback_compensated, rollback_target_unbootable, compensation_incomplete). Use to escape a bad deploy after the swap_rollback window has closed.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: RestartResult envelope with status, restart_action_id, message, reason, expected_etag, dry_run, and the machine-readable reason_code partition field.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with status. If 'queued', surface restart_action_id (the pollable complete_swap finisher) + the reactivated release. If 'failed', surface message + reason_code — the system is unchanged and the operator may retry. If 'needs_intervention', surface message + reason_code prominently — automated recovery is exhausted and a human must act (the rollback target will not boot, or the durable current/previous pair may be incoherent).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Operator-triggered durable code rollback to the prior local blue-green release.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: status='failed' with reason_code is NOT a crash — it is a coherent retryable refusal (stale_current_release: the live current release moved since the caller observed it — the concurrency CAS, checked FIRST; no_rollback_target: no previous release to roll back to; activate_refused: the router refused the previous color, current still active). status='needs_intervention' means automated recovery is exhausted: rollback_target_unbootable (the previous release dir is gone/corrupt or never registered within the timeout — the safety net is void) or compensation_incomplete (a failed swap's compensation could not complete, so the durable pair MAY be incoherent).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: On 'failed', address the named cause and retry (on stale_current_release, re-read the live current_release — swap_status surfaces it — and retry with that value; confirm this instance is the router-active one). On 'needs_intervention', do NOT retry blindly — inspect the on-disk releases under ~/.ananta/releases/<name>/ (current/previous symlinks + state.json ledger). The cold-boot fallback for a dead the solet is out-of-band: call ReleaseManager.rollback() then re-launch via ananta.cli, which cold-boots whatever current now points at.
